lens: Recheck R-001 and inspect related claims in the notes and docs against the selected sandbox code and tests.

findings.summary: The notes and docs give an incomplete list of exceptions to other host Unix sockets staying reachable.
evidence: Both the notes and docs say such sockets stay reachable unless they are under /run/user/<uid> or under /tmp outside restored temporary trees.
sandbox_prefix also masks existing home directories such as ~/.ssh and ~/.config with read-only tmpfs mounts, so a host Unix socket under one of those directories would not stay reachable.
findings.action: Qualify both reachability claims to include sockets under other masked home paths.

counterweight_triage.concern: R-001: the unit-test fixture was described as a stand-in socket.
counterweight_triage.disposition: The notes now accurately call it a stand-in file at a socket path; the test creates a regular file and checks the emitted --ro-bind. The notes also correctly say no test pins the other daemon paths or /run/user/<uid> mask.

counterweight_triage.concern: Other host Unix sockets are described as reachable except under /run/user/<uid> and certain /tmp paths.
counterweight_triage.disposition: The code masks additional home paths, including ~/.ssh and ~/.config.

next_move: Revise the notes and docs to include other masked home paths among the exceptions to socket reachability.
non_claims: This review assessed the supplied identity-bound content and did not execute tests or sandbox behavior.
Coverage observations are limited to the selected files.
